newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Media mogul Black wants half of Australia's Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: Media mogul Black wants half of Australia's Fairfax.

text.p: Canadian media baron Conrad Black said Wednesday he wanted to increase his stake in Australia's oldest newspaper group, John Fairfax Holdings Ltd., to 50 percent from 25 percent.
But the media baron said he would sell out of Fairfax unless Australia eased its current media ownership rules.

Foreigners cannot own more than 25 percent of a newspaper group or 15 percent of a television group under the current law. The rules also prevent a newspaper group owner from holding more than 15 percent of a television station in the same city.
"These things as they are now are very anachronistic," Black told reporters.
His current stake is held through Toronto-based Hollinger International Inc.
Black, 52, has consistently sought a higher stake in Fairfax since leading a consortium in 1991 to buy Fairfax out of receivership.
"There is an instability about the future for all Fairfax employees and all the Fairfax observers know that," Black said, referring to regular takeover rumours about Fairfax.

Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer, has a 15 percent stake in Fairfax through his media empire Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd., while fellow media baron Rupert Murdoch owns 5 percent of Fairfax through his News Corp. media group.

Packer has said previously he would like to own Fairfax, while Murdoch, who controls 66 percent of Australia's metropolitan newspaper circulation, has described Fairfax's classified advertising revenue as "rivers of gold."

Black told shareholders at Fairfax's annual meeting that he had told Prime Minister John Howard on Tuesday, in their first meeting since Howard won election in March, that he would like to raise his stake in the newspaper group.
